wording: P99 finds that prosocial participants (social value orientation, 1151 of 1655) endorse self-transcendence values, Universalism and Benevolence, more strongly than individualists and competitors, and Power values less strongly (largest effects Universalism eta^2 .037 and Power .040). P99 cautions that combining Universalism and Benevolence into a higher-order Self-transcendence score can obscure differences between them.
locator: P99 Introduction to Discussion, Tables 1-3 (read in full)
confidence: Moderate (one sample of 1655 university students; cross-sectional)
counterevidence_limits: Student sample; small effects. Slips: the Results text says pro-socials endorsed Conformity 'less strongly' although Table 3's means (-.513 vs -.692 and -.675) and the planned comparison show the opposite; Table 2 prints Power's mean as .469 (Universalism's value); see TR0-SOC-02.
operationalization: SOC Transcendence = self-transcendence values and prosocial orientation
verification_phrases: P99|1151 (69.5%) were classified as prosocial || P99|typically labelled as Self-transcendence || P99|pro-socials endorsed Conformity, Hedonism, Achievement, and Power values less strongly
change_vs_prev_cycle: carried from TR0-SOC-01 unchanged (sources read in full in TR0; not re-read in TRA)

wording: Most of P99's printed numbers reproduce: 1151 + 381 + 123 = 1655 (69.5, 23.0, 7.4%), every main-effect and planned-comparison eta^2 from F and df (largest gap 0.0005), every printed p within 0.002. Two pre-registered checks were not supported: the Results participant flow (1906 - 223 - 23) gives 1660, not the analysed 1655 (the Method flow 1903 - 226 - 22 gives 1655); and the n-weighted Table 3 means reproduce Table 2 for ten values but give -0.524 for Power where Table 2 prints .469. Also: competitors are 7.4% (text elsewhere 7.3%); critical r .048 and .063 (printed .049, .064).
counterevidence_limits: Audits printed rounded numbers; error df n - 3 from each row's n is the agent's assumption.
operationalization: SOC Transcendence = auditing a values study
change_vs_prev_cycle: carried from TR0-SOC-02 unchanged (sources read in full in TR0; not re-read in TRA)

wording: At P99's unequal group sizes (1151, 381, 123) a one-way ANOVA detects a Universalism-sized effect (eta^2 .037) essentially always (power 1.00) but a Security-sized effect (eta^2 .003) only about half the time (Monte Carlo 0.510, noncentral F 0.501), so P99's non-significant small effects are not evidence of no difference.
confidence: High (4000 replicates; agrees with noncentral F)
counterevidence_limits: Normal data with unit SD and Table 3's mean pattern assumed.
operationalization: SOC Transcendence = power of the values comparisons

wording: P99's five G*Power statements reproduce (0.962, 0.963, 0.998, 0.921, 0.486 vs .96, .96, .99, .92, .49). Universalism means are ordered prosocial > individualist > competitor, but one pre-registered check was not supported: for the first Benevolence measure competitors (.667) score above individualists (.558), so self-transcendence values do not rank the three SVO groups the same way, consistent with P99's caution against a combined Self-transcendence score.
counterevidence_limits: Ordering of printed means only; no test of the individualist-competitor difference is recomputed.
operationalization: SOC Transcendence = auditing power and orderings
